definition: An epileptogenic focus is the specific brain area where epileptic seizure activity starts. In focal epilepsy, identifying this seizure-onset location can help relate symptoms, including autonomic changes, to the brain structures involved.

reasons: The requested field is not defensible from the packet: this is an epilepsy/neurology topic about focal seizures and autonomic dysfunction, not a cognition entry.

The definition makes a specific causal claim that an epileptogenic focus is the exact brain area where seizure activity starts; the packet supports identifying epileptogenic focus locations and brain structures associated with seizures, but does not explicitly define the term in those words.

The definition’s first sentence (“specific brain area where epileptic seizure activity starts”) is broadly consistent with the packet’s use of “epileptogenic focus locations or brain structures” and its focus on seizure-onset/epileptogenic localization, but the packet does not provide an explicit one-to-one definitional statement of “epileptogenic focus” as “the specific brain area where seizure activity starts.”

The second sentence claims that identifying the seizure-onset location “can help relate symptoms, including autonomic changes, to the brain structures involved.” While the packet discusses autonomic changes during seizures and argues that ictal autonomic dysfunction indicates involvement of central autonomic areas and may be useful diagnostically, it does not explicitly state that *identifying the epileptogenic focus/seizure-onset location* helps relate symptoms to brain structures in the way the definition asserts.
